original_registry_entry.issuing_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
original_registry_entry.exact_document_title: Food allergy in under 19s: assessment and diagnosis
original_registry_entry.version: NICE clinical guideline CG116, published 2011 and last reviewed 2018
original_registry_entry.jurisdiction: England, United Kingdom; international guidance requiring UAE adaptation
original_registry_entry.population: Children and young people under 19 with suspected food allergy.
original_registry_entry.clinical_setting: Primary, community and specialist food-allergy assessment.
original_registry_entry.applicability_note: Exact for allergy-focused history, symptom and exposure context, physical examination, clinician-selected testing, information and referral documentation. It does not diagnose allergy, select an elimination plan or generate emergency treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.4 — assessment and allergy-focused clinical history
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting symptom systems, age and speed of onset, duration, severity, frequency, setting, reproducibility, suspected food, exposure amount, atopic and feeding history, prior treatment and growth or examination findings.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.5–1.1.11 — IgE-mediated and non-IgE-mediated diagnosis
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording clinician-selected skin-prick or specific-IgE testing, test limitations, elimination and reintroduction discussion and result review without interpreting results or generating treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.12 and referral recommendations — information, support and specialist care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting information about suspected allergy, severe-reaction risk, diagnostic process, support and clinician-entered referral or follow-up.
